before.title: 7-speed dry-clutch DSG (DQ200) mechatronic and clutch-pack failures
before.description: Superbs fitted with the 7-speed dry-clutch DSG (DQ200/0AM, used behind the 1.4 TSI and lower-output engines on Mk2 3T and Mk3 3V) commonly develop dual-clutch and mechatronic faults. Owners report a metallic squeal/judder on 1st-2nd and 2nd-3rd shifts, the box holding a gear (e.g. staying in 3rd through corners), jerky low-speed engagement, and in worse cases warning lights, limp mode or complete loss of drive. The root causes are the dry clutch pack wearing/contaminating and the mechatronic valve body, whose thin-walled pressure accumulator can crack and lose hydraulic pressure. Skoda/VW issued a technical instruction (TPI 2042705/5) for the squeal symptom, with dealers replacing the clutch pack.
before.solution: Have the box diagnosed for stored mechatronic codes. Common remedies are replacing the dual-clutch pack (per Skoda TPI for the squeal), or repairing/replacing the mechatronic unit if the accumulator/valve body has failed. A DSG service (oil and filter where applicable) and avoiding prolonged clutch slip in stop-start traffic reduce wear. Many cases on cars in warranty are covered; out of warranty, specialist mechatronic/clutch rebuilds are far cheaper than a new unit.
symptoms: Metallic squeal or judder on 1st-2nd and 2nd-3rd shifts
Gearbox holds a gear / won't change on corners
Limp mode or loss of drive

before.title: Columbus infotainment freezes, shutdowns and reboot loops
before.description: Both Mk2 and Mk3 Superbs are widely reported to have unreliable infotainment. On the Mk3, the Columbus head unit (satnav, Bluetooth, CD, DAB/TV) has been documented shutting down or freezing, the screen entering reboot loops, pre-set radio stations being lost when the engine is switched off, erroneous satnav directions, and the aux/iPod connection intermittently dropping out, with Skoda at times having no fix available. The same Columbus shutdown behaviour was noted as carried over from the previous-generation Superb.
before.solution: Try a head-unit/MIB software update at a Skoda dealer, which resolves many freeze/reboot and Bluetooth issues; a hard reset can clear temporary lockups. Persistent hardware faults require head-unit repair or replacement. Check for any infotainment TPIs for the build year.

before.title: Diesel particulate filter (DPF) clogging and regeneration failure
before.description: The 2.0 TDI diesels (Mk2 and Mk3) suffer DPF problems, especially on cars used mainly for short, low-speed urban trips that never allow the filter to complete a regeneration. Symptoms include a DPF warning, repeated/incomplete active regenerations, raised idle, and rising sump oil level (and falling fuel economy) because diesel from post-injection regen dilutes the engine oil. Owners report DPFs needing replacement at relatively low mileage (e.g. ~52,000 miles). Active regen contaminating the oil was specifically noted by dealers on Mk3 2.0 TDI cars.
before.solution: Take the car for a sustained motorway run at higher revs to complete a regeneration when the DPF light appears. If the filter is clogged, a forced regen via diagnostics or a professional DPF clean may recover it; otherwise replace the DPF. Change engine oil if it has been fuel-diluted by repeated regens, and choose a non-DPF/petrol/PHEV variant for short-trip use.
symptoms: Rising engine oil level / oil dilution

before.title: EA888 Gen2 petrol oil consumption and stretched timing chain
before.description: Mk2 (3T) Superbs with the second-generation EA888 1.8 TSI and 2.0 TSI petrol engines are well documented for excessive oil consumption and a timing-chain that stretches. Oil burning is caused by undersized/poorly-draining piston rings and can reach roughly 0.5-2 litres per 1,000 km as mileage climbs past ~100,000 km. Separately, the camshaft timing chain and its tensioner wear, allowing the chain to stretch around 60,000-100,000 miles; this produces a cold-start rattle, rough running, and risk of chain jump and severe valve/piston damage if ignored. Gen3 engines (from ~2012) received a revised tensioner and are far less prone.
before.solution: Monitor oil level frequently and keep it topped up. For chronic oil burning the fix is replacing pistons/rings with revised parts; check for any applicable VW oil-consumption goodwill. For the chain, replace the timing chain, tensioner and guides as a preventive job the moment a cold-start rattle appears, before the chain jumps. Use the correct VW 504.00 long-life oil and don't extend oil-change intervals.
symptoms: High oil consumption / frequent topping up

before.title: Electromechanical parking brake sticking and rapid rear disc/pad wear
before.description: Mk3 Superbs have documented problems with the electromechanical (electronic) parking brake and rear brakes. Owners report the EPB sticking/dragging and accelerated rear-brake wear, including corroded, pitted or scored rear discs and worn pads at low mileage (reported around 20,000-27,000 miles). At least one owner reported Skoda eventually issued a recall related to the parking brake roughly 23 months after the initial complaint, with some dealers initially classifying disc corrosion as wear-and-tear.
before.solution: Have the electronic parking brake actuators/calipers inspected and serviced (the rear calipers can seize). Replace corroded/scored discs and pads as needed and ensure any applicable Skoda recall/TPI on the parking brake has been carried out. Periodic light use of the handbrake on dry roads helps keep rear discs clean.
symptoms: Corroded, pitted or scored rear brake discs

before.description: Skoda Superb Mk2 (3T) 2.0 TDI common-rail diesels built roughly between 2009 and 2011 were subject to a safety recall because faulty material allowed the high-pressure fuel pipes to develop leaks during service life, a fire/leak hazard. before.title: P2015 intake manifold swirl-flap actuator failure (2.0 TDI CR)
before.description: The 2.0 TDI Common Rail diesel (shared across Skoda Superb, Octavia and Yeti) very commonly logs fault code P2015 - intake manifold flap position sensor. The plastic swirl-flap lever/runner inside the inlet manifold and the V157 actuator motor wear and go out of range, so the ECU can no longer verify flap position. This triggers the EML, can put the car into reduced power/limp mode and hurts running. The official VW remedy historically was a complete intake manifold, which is expensive.
before.solution: Diagnose with VCDS to confirm P2015 / 008213. The economical fix is an aftermarket aluminium repair bracket that limits the V157 actuator motor's travel back to the original range, restoring correct flap position; otherwise replace the intake manifold assembly. Clearing carbon and checking the actuator wiring is worthwhile at the same time.

before.title: Water ingress through blocked plenum drains causing wet footwells and electrical faults
before.description: A recurring complaint across Superb generations is water leaking into the cabin, typically the front passenger footwell, when the plenum chamber/scuttle drains beneath the windscreen become blocked with leaves and debris. Water can also reach the pollen/cabin filter housing. Standing water and damp wiring (including looms and modules under the carpet/scuttle) can trigger intermittent electrical gremlins. A separate documented Mk3 electrical issue (cars built May-Dec 2015) is an incorrectly fitted cable clamp in the under-fuse-box area causing many electrical functions to stop working.
before.solution: Clear leaves and debris from the plenum/scuttle drain channels and check the drain holes flow freely; reseal the pollen-filter housing if water is entering there. Dry out and inspect any affected wiring/modules. For the 2015 build electrical fault, fit the corrected cable clamp per Skoda's parts list. Keep the scuttle area clear seasonally to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Wet front passenger footwell / damp carpet

before.title: EA888 Plastic Water Pump and Thermostat Housing Failure
before.description: Mk2 and Mk3 Superb with EA888 1.8/2.0 TSI engines suffer the same plastic water pump and thermostat housing failure as VW/Audi siblings. The plastic body cracks, causing coolant leaks. Often happens around 80,000-120,000 mi.
before.solution: Replace water pump + thermostat housing as a unit (€350-€600 parts). Best done with timing belt service if not done recently.
